original_question: Let f(n) be the maximum number of edges in a graph on n vertices in which no two cycles have the same length. Does the lower asymptotic normalized gap satisfy lim inf_{n→∞} (f(n) − n)/√n ≤ √2.4?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.6 (Lai [31]) in Section 1, "Erdős Problem 1," stated after Theorem 1.3 and Conjecture 1.4 as one of the paper's weaker conjectures about f(n). ([archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/pacm_download/168/4692-cycle.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper very closely: it uses the paper's definition of f(n) as the maximum number of edges in a graph on n vertices with no two cycles of the same length, and it asks exactly for the lim inf inequality with constant √2.4 that appears in Conjecture 1.6. ([archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/pacm_download/168/4692-cycle.pdf))
missing_details: The paper's official target is specifically Conjecture 1.6, not the stronger Conjecture 1.4; that contextual placement is missing from the draft. ([archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/pacm_download/168/4692-cycle.pdf))

For full stand-alone precision, say explicitly that n ranges over positive integers and that the limit inferior is taken as n → ∞ through integer values of n. The paper states the asymptotic claim in that standard discrete sense. ([archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/pacm_download/168/4692-cycle.pdf))

The phrase "lower asymptotic normalized gap" is not paper language; the official formulation is simply the lim inf statement itself. ([archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/pacm_download/168/4692-cycle.pdf))

The nearby context matters: Theorem 1.3 gives the lower bound f(n) ≥ n + √2.4 √n (1 - o(1)), and Conjecture 1.4 asks for the stronger conclusion that the full limit equals √2.4; Conjecture 1.6 is presented only as a weaker conjecture. ([archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/pacm_download/168/4692-cycle.pdf))
refined_question: Let f(n) denote the maximum number of edges in a graph on n vertices in which all cycles have pairwise distinct lengths. Is it true that, as n → ∞ through the positive integers, lim inf ((f(n) - n)/√n) ≤ √2.4? ([archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/pacm_download/168/4692-cycle.pdf))
justification: Section 1 first defines f(n), then records Theorem 1.3, which gives the lower bound with leading constant √2.4, then states the stronger Conjecture 1.4 that the full normalized limit equals √2.4, and immediately afterward says that proving that seems difficult and proposes weaker Conjectures 1.5 and 1.6. Because your draft asks exactly whether lim inf_{n→∞}(f(n)-n)/√n ≤ √2.4, it is targeting Conjecture 1.6 and not a broader neighboring problem. ([archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/pacm_download/168/4692-cycle.pdf))
